newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex sees property income continuing.
newsitem.headline: Vendex sees property income continuing.

text.p: Income from redevelopment and sales of real estate will remain important for Dutch retail and services group Vendex's profits in coming years, Vendex International NV chairman Jan-Michiel Hessels said on Tuesday.
Property-related income amounted to 111 million guilders in 1996/97, down from 126 million guilders the previous year.
Hessels said the income had to be split up between that originating from the redevelopment of owned property, and other property income through sale and lease back.
He said redevelopment of property would result in an average annual profit of some 35 million guilders in future years, against some 40 million in 1996/97.
Other property income, from sale and lease back of property, would also remain substantial in the current financial year, Hessels said.
Earlier on Tuesday, Vendex announced a 30 percent rise in 1996/97 total net profit to 539 million guilders, while turnover totalled 12.145 billion guilders.
Operating income amounted to 473 million guilders, of which 111 million was property related.
Hessels said he preferred to look at the operating profit figure excluding property income.

"The figure excluding property-related income is a purer measure of the state of things. We have many years to go, but at a certain moment, it (income from property) will come to an end," Hessels said.
